Checks on this run

All five controllers

Algorithm-level, quasi-static simulation. Iterations are not seconds. Tracking efficiency is not converter efficiency.

Model equations & measurement alignment

Single-diode PV model: I = Iph − I₀[exp((V + I Rs) / Vt) − 1] − (V + I Rs) / Rsh. Parameters come from the original project's numerical fit.

Ideal CCM boost: Rin = (1 − D)² Rload; Vout = Vpv / (1 − D). The PV curve and load line determine the operating point.

Dynamic model in the project: L diL/dt = Vpv − (1 − D)Vout; Cout dVout/dt = (1 − D)iL − Vout/Rload. These transients are not integrated in the MPPT comparisons.

Alignment: circuit readings use the duty applied for the measurement, D(k). The duty chart shows the controller's returned command, D(k + 1), matching the report plots. HOLD stops duty perturbations, not PWM switching.

Noisy runs: interactive traces use one displayed NumPy seed; the report noise table averages eight seeds. Floating-point differences in long RLS runs can slightly change the browser trajectories. The archived values remain unchanged.

Known boundaries: placeholder 36-cell panel; ideal lossless converter; ESR and switching losses unknown; hardware validation pending. Cin and sensing chains belong to the circuit, but their dynamics and losses are not included in the algebraic model. Partial shading uses three series substrings with −0.7 V bypass clamps; the source schematic represents the PV module as one block.

Metrics: full-run efficiency = mean(P/Pmpp); steady-state efficiency uses the last 50 iterations; activity = fraction of active perturbation samples; oscillation = peak-to-peak returned duty over the last 50 iterations. The source's sampled MPP reference can give tiny numerical values above 100%. No physical energy in joules is claimed without an iteration period.

MODEL VALIDITY / AVERAGED CONVERTER DYNAMICS

How long does the circuit take to settle?

Apply a duty step to the project's averaged boost model and inspect the physical transient.

A test of the MPPT assumption

The controller experiments assume that the converter settles between updates. This independent experiment holds the source voltage constant and integrates the original boost ODE. It reveals the timescale hidden by the quasi-static model; it is not a fully coupled PV–converter simulation.

Duty-step experiment

Starts at the initial steady state. Duty changes at 50 ms. L = 220 µH, Cout = 671 µF. No ESR, switching ripple or losses.

Equations
L diL/dt = Vin − (1 − D)Vout
Cout dVout/dt = (1 − D)iL − Vout/R

Output voltage

V · dashed line = final equilibrium

Inductor current

A · step at 50 ms

Settling time is measured after the step until both current and voltage stay within 1% of their final values for the remainder of the 300 ms simulation. It is not an MPPT convergence time. A negative computed current means the CCM equations have left their physical range; no DCM model is substituted.

REPRODUCIBLE EVIDENCE / SIX EXPERIMENTS

Make the comparison stand up to questions.

Run a fixed benchmark protocol and inspect the efficiency–activity trade-off.

100 controller runs

Five controllers across six scenarios. Eight seeds for each noisy experiment; one for each deterministic experiment.

Matched conditions

Same source equations, initial duty and noise stream per seed. SEARCH retains the original clean-probe assumption.

No single “best” score

Efficiency and activity stay separate. A controller can improve one and lose on the other.

Ready. This suite uses fixed project settings, independent of the controller-lab sliders.

What the project contributes

Duty-space estimation: RLS estimates the local power gradient online.

Confidence with a slope gate: a stable fit alone does not justify HOLD; the estimated gradient must also be small.

State persistence: consecutive qualifying samples reduce rapid state changes.

Ablation evidence: each stage isolates the effect of adding one mechanism.

Claims you can defend

Supported: fewer duty perturbations in stable conditions, with a quantified tracking-efficiency trade-off.

Not established: lower hardware switching loss, guaranteed global MPP tracking, or field-proven reliability.

Next engineering milestone: couple the dynamic PV–converter model to the controller at a justified sample period; then compare against measured V/I traces from the PCB.

Research extension: investigate an independent peak check to detect confident local-peak traps, counting its scan-energy cost in the comparison.

Read the results with their limits

The full controller shares HOLD/TRACK's clean baseline result because SEARCH is not needed in that experiment. Under sustained measurement noise, activity reduction can disappear. Under partial shading, high confidence can also occur at a local peak: the archived Monte Carlo study reports a 52% trap rate across its 50 shaded scenarios. The website preserves these limitations.

The SEARCH noise-burst validation in the supplied code does not fix its random seed; its original figure is preserved here. New interactive runs use a visible, reproducible seed and may not match that figure point-for-point.
